recentItems.title: Is AI erasing your neighborhood? | Angela Pitter | TEDxRoxbury
recentItems.description:
AI won’t replace us, but it will erase communities that don’t actively teach it who they are. Neighborhoods like Roxbury can become the blueprint for stopping that erasure. Algorithmic equity begins at the neighborhood level, and the communities that act now will write the rules for those that follow. Neighborhoods can intentionally 'train' AI by creating a coordinated digital blueprint: structured stories, cultural markers, and institutional signals that teach algorithms who we are.  

Angela Pitter builds digital visibility for the organizations and neighborhoods that algorithms overlook. As Founder & CEO of LiveWire Collaborative, an AI and digital strategy firm, she serves large nonprofits and mid-sized organizations navigating AI's impact on their communities and credibility. Angela's path runs from Bronx Science to a Computer Engineering degree at Boston University to 25 years of global technology leadership, before she pivoted to mission-driven work across Greater Boston. She blends deep technical fluency with a sharp understanding of how storytelling, place, and data determine which communities get seen and which are skipped. Angela serves as the Board Chair of the Charles River Regional Chamber and has been recognized as a Commonwealth Heroine and one of Massachusetts' 50 Most Influential Business People of Color. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Problem Isn’t the Problem  | Jessica Diaz | TEDxClaremont Graduate University
recentItems.description: When something goes wrong, we rush to fix it. But too often, nothing changes, not because we lack solutions, but because we never stopped to ask what was actually broken. In this talk, organizational psychologist Jessica Diaz introduces a deceptively simple framework that reveals what’s underneath the problems we keep trying to solve: when things aren’t working as intended, it almost always traces back to one of three root causes, a gap in knowledge, skill, or mindset. Drawing on two decades of work with leaders and organizations, and one memorable refrigerator incident, Diaz shows how a misaligned solution doesn’t just fail to fix the problem, it quietly creates new ones. The people with the greatest power to solve our most pressing problems aren’t the ones who always have the answer, they’re the ones willing to turn the framework on themselves first. Because in doing so, they shape the conditions that determine whether anything actually changes. Jessica Diaz, Ph.D., is an organizational psychologist focused on helping leaders diagnose and reshape the conditions driving employee experience and performance. She is a professor & researcher at Claremont Graduate University, where she directs ExCo: The Employee Experience Collective, a research and practice lab dedicated to advancing authentic and empowered experiences at work. With over two decades of experience leading teams and developing people, she partners with organizations to strengthen leadership, culture, and the underlying systems that shape how work gets done. Jessica’s approach blends rigorous research with practical tools, grounded in data and systems thinking, to help leaders move beyond quick fixes and get to what’s actually driving results. She is known for helping leaders see patterns others miss and for making complex challenges understandable and actionable. Her work helps leaders move beyond surface-level solutions to address the conditions that shape outcomes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Build: Self-Actualization is a System, Not Magic | Justin Vazquez | TEDxJeffersonU
recentItems.description:
Justin Vazquez is a Creative Director at Eidos-Montréal with over 25 years of experience designing stories and systems across music, film, television, and video games. Most recently, he led the creative direction for Grounded 2, the critically acclaimed sequel developed in collaboration with Obsidian Entertainment. He is also the author of The Build: A System for Self-Actualization, where he applies decades of experience designing systems that shape player behavior to the challenge of human growth.

In his TEDx talk, The Build: Self-Actualization is a System, Not Magic, Justin challenges the cultural myth that success inevitably requires sacrifice. Drawing on lessons from game design, psychology, music, elite performance, and his own journey through cancer, divorce, developing Grounded 2, and rebuilding his life, he presents a practical framework built on three trainable pillars: Autonomy, Mastery, and Harmony. By replacing shame with diagnosis and treating personal growth as a system rather than a mystery, Justin offers a blueprint for building a life capable of sustaining both achievement and fulfillment. recentItems.title: Is  this a share or a fix? | Dympna Weil | TEDxJeffersonU
recentItems.description: Dympna Weil, MD, is a physician and writer who spent two decades as a board-certified OBGYN before a vestibular disorder ended her clinical practice in 2020. A Master Certified Coach and founder of Prescribing Possibility, her writing and expertise have appeared in The New York Times' Modern Love, Newsweek, and Parade. In her TEDx talk, she explores a question she now asks in nearly every hard conversation: is this a share, or a fix? Drawing on medicine and motherhood, she offers a simple diagnostic that changes what happens when someone is struggling and what real help looks like. recentItems.title: Re-entry injury: A speech on returning | Jamal Benson | TEDxJeffersonU
recentItems.description: This speech explores the concept of "re-entry injury": the emotional wound and identity struggle that occurs when returning to a former environment after personal growth. Through his personal journey as a second-generation Nigerian American, Jamal Benson illustrates this phenomenon, from a traumatic childhood visit to Nigeria that left him with a physical scar, to a painful adult return where he felt like an outsider in his parents' homeland. Jamal introduces a four-pillar healing framework called ROOT—Recognition, Openness, Ownership, and Touchstones—designed to help navigate these emotional returns. Ultimately, Jamal discovers that healing from re-entry injury isn't about erasing the past but about reclaiming authorship of one's own narrative and understanding that while the wound may not fully heal, the journey itself is a direction worth pursuing. recentItems.title: Forget your nouns. Find your verbs | Cảnh Luân Nguyễn | TEDxLuong The Vinh Youth
recentItems.description:
As high school students, we are often asked, “What do you want to be?” At an age when the future can feel both exciting and overwhelming, we are expected to choose a single noun to define who we are: a doctor, a designer, a teacher, an entrepreneur. But what if we are asking the wrong question? Drawing from his own journey across education, content creation, writing, poetry, acting, and music, Nguyễn Cảnh Luân explores how seemingly unrelated interests can come together to form a meaningful direction. Rather than defining ourselves by the titles we hold, he invites us to look deeper at the verbs that keep appearing throughout our experiences - the things we love to explain, create, express, connect, or solve. Through this perspective, our different interests become less like scattered choices and more like notes in the same song. Forget your nouns. Find your verbs.
 Nguyễn Cảnh Luân is an educator, content creator, author, and creative artist whose work spans language, education, knowledge sharing, and the arts. A graduate of RMIT University and Foreign Trade University, he began his career in education and founded Language for Life, where he teaches English, communication, and presentation skills.

He is the author of the IELTS Speaking Journey 6.0 and 8.0 book series, and has built a strong presence as a content creator through accessible content on language, science, everyday knowledge, and personal development. His signature phrase, “I do the research so you don’t have to,” reflects his passion for making knowledge engaging and accessible.

Beyond education and digital content, he explores poetry, music, acting, and public speaking. His bilingual poetry collection, “Someone Would Love Me for Me,” further reflects his distinctive approach to language as both a tool for learning and a form of creative expression. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Future Opera | António Wagner Diniz, Mariana Lourenço Chaves & Pedro Vieira de Almeida | TEDxMarvila
recentItems.description:
He opens the talk mid-performance — a live aria from The Magic Flute, the same one he teaches in classrooms across Portugal. António Wagner Diniz spent decades as an opera singer and ran Lisbon's National Conservatory; now he spends his time bringing music into schools in the country's poorest neighborhoods. The moment worth waiting for: a story about a five-year-old who watched two singers perform an argument in song and immediately recognized it as her own parents fighting at home. It's a small moment that says everything about why he believes opera isn't just entertainment — it's a way for children to finally see feelings they don't yet have words for. Watch it, and see why he thinks the future needs more of this, not less. António Wagner Diniz holds degrees in Economics and Music and has built a distinguished career as an opera singer, musical performer, and cultural animator since 1975. His most notable social and musical projects include Orquestra Geração – El Sistema Portugal and Opera nas Escolas. A visionary educator and cultural advocate, he transforms young lives through collective music making, proving that harmony is a learned skill.

Mariana Lourenço Chaves was Born March 20, 2004, Mariana Chaves holds a bachelor's degree in Opera Singing from the Escola Superior de Música de Lisboa, where she studied under Professor Sílvia Mateus, and is currently pursuing a master's in Voice Pedagogy at the same institution under Professor Siphiwe Mackenzie. She began singing at age 4 in the choir of Casa do Povo de Corroios and later performed with the Coro Juvenil de Lisboa in opera productions at Teatro Nacional de São Carlos. She was a semifinalist on Got Talent Portugal and a finalist on TVI's Funtastico, bringing classical music to the show's live galas. Since 2022 she has been a regular cast member of the Companhia de Ópera de Setúbal.

Born in Coimbra in 1979, Pedro Vieira de Almeida graduated in Piano in 2002 from the Escola Superior de Música de Lisboa. In 2004 he began a Master's in Musical Arts, specializing in Chamber Music, jointly offered by NOVA University Lisbon and the Escola Superior de Música de Lisboa, completing it with the highest distinction. He won awards at the Portuguese Musical Youth Piano Competition (1995) and the Young Musicians Prize Chamber Music Competition (2002), and has maintained an active concert career across Portugal, recording three CDs with saxophonist João Pedro Silva. He has also worked in film, television, and theatre, notably in the original play Ninguém Morre a Cantar by Rui Pina Coelho, alongside actress and singer Sara Belo. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Nothing is wasted | Đạo Đạo Lâm | TEDxLuong The Vinh Youth
recentItems.description:
Từ một cậu học sinh cấp ba chưa biết tương lai sẽ đi về đâu, Lâm Đạo Đạo bắt đầu hành trình sáng tạo bằng sự tò mò và những sở thích tưởng chừng chẳng liên quan: nhảy, nhiếp ảnh, hội họa, nội thất, âm nhạc hay DJ. Những trải nghiệm ấy từng bước đưa anh đến với vai trò Creative Director & Director, đồng hành cùng nhiều nghệ sĩ và thương hiệu lớn, cũng như góp phần tạo nên những dự án vươn ra quốc tế. Qua câu chuyện của mình, Lâm Đạo Đạo sẽ cùng chúng ta nhìn lại cách những điều tưởng như “vô bổ” lại có thể trở thành chất liệu để mở rộng góc nhìn, nuôi dưỡng tư duy sáng tạo và tạo nên dấu ấn riêng. Bởi đôi khi, ta không cần biết trước tất cả những điểm đến; chỉ cần đủ tò mò để bước đi, những mảnh ghép tưởng chừng rời rạc rồi sẽ tìm được cách kết nối với nhau. Không có trải nghiệm nào là vô nghĩa, nếu ta biết cách biến chúng thành một phần của chính mình.
 Lâm Đạo Đạo is a Vietnamese Director known for his distinctive visual storytelling across the music and film industries. Since beginning his directing career in 2014, he has worked with prominent Vietnamese artists including Wren Evans, tlinh, HIEUTHUHAI, SOOBIN, and Vũ Cát Tường, creating music videos that blend each artist’s identity with his own artistic vision.

His work has received major recognition, including a Gold Award at VTV Bài hát tôi yêu 2016 for the music video “Mơ” and two major awards in 2025 for “Giá Như” with SOOBIN: Most Favorite MV at the Mai Vàng Awards and MV of the Year at the Dedication Music Awards.

As a member of Zorba The Imaginary Friend, he also won the 48-Hour Film Project Vietnam in 2019 and later represented Vietnam at Filmapalooza USA. His work on “Inside the Yellow Cocoon Shell” contributed to the film’s journey to Cannes 2023, where it received the prestigious Camera d’Or. recentItems.title: English anxiety is real? | Minh Như Trần Nguyễn | TEDxLuong The Vinh Youth
recentItems.description:
For many students, English begins as something they are expected to learn rather than something they genuinely want to explore. Surrounded by grades, exams, comparison, and expectations, a language meant to connect us with the world can gradually become a source of pressure and anxiety. Drawing from her own experience preparing for the National Excellent Student Competition in English, Trần Nguyễn Minh Như reflects on how she moved from feeling intimidated and inadequate to finding her own reason to keep learning. Through her story, she invites us to look beyond scores and achievements, and to reconsider what truly keeps us moving forward when external motivation is no longer enough. Perhaps overcoming the fear of English does not begin with becoming the best, but with finding something within the language that makes us want to take the next step. Let curiosity guide you, and let English grow with you - not as a burden to carry, but as a bridge to the world and to yourself.
 Trần Nguyễn Minh Như is a high school student at Luong The Vinh High School for the Gifted with a strong passion for English, community projects, and public speaking. She holds an IELTS 8.0 and has received awards in national, provincial, and regional English competitions, including First Prize at the 2025–2026 Provincial Excellent Student Competition and a Silver Medal at the April 30th Olympic Competition.

Beyond academics, Minh Như is the Founder of Góc Phổ, a project supporting people on the autism spectrum. She is also a member of her school’s Youth Union Executive Committee and an Outstanding Youth Union Member for 2025–2026.

At TEDxYouth Luong The Vinh 2026: Harmony, she shares her perspective on embracing challenges, navigating academic pressure, and finding harmony through growth. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Finding myself beyond the crown  | Quỳnh Như Lê Thị | TEDxLuong The Vinh Youth
recentItems.description:
Growing up, we are often taught to measure ourselves through grades, achievements, and the people around us. For Lê Thị Quỳnh Như, that habit once made her feel as though no achievement was ever quite enough. Even when she was doing well, she was still looking sideways, wondering if she was good enough compared to everyone else. Her journey through competitions, English, and public speaking gradually taught her to see things differently: that finding yourself is not about becoming the most outstanding person in the crowd, but about understanding what makes you uniquely you. In her talk, Quỳnh Như reflects on the journey from comparison to self-discovery, and how embracing our differences can help us grow with greater confidence and purpose. Because sometimes, finding your place is not about fitting into the crowd, but finding the courage to discover who you are beyond it.
 Le Thi Quynh Nhu is a student from English Specialized Class 1 at Luong The Vinh High School for the Gifted. She has actively challenged herself through academic and public speaking competitions, earning the Top 3 entrance score of her cohort and several notable achievements, including Champion of Cuộc Chiến Vương Quyền 2025, First Runner-up at I-Transform IV and the LTV English Speaking Contest: Speak Up Challenge 2026, as well as Silver and Bronze Medals at the National IOE.

Beyond academic achievements, Quynh Nhu is passionate about personal growth and finding her own path amid expectations and self-doubt. At TEDxYouth Luong The Vinh 2026: Harmony, she shares her journey of learning to embrace her individuality and find harmony within herself. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Story that shape us | Renita Santo | TEDxTIPS Salem Youth
recentItems.description: The speech explores how culture, family, traditions, relocation, friendships, challenges, and personal experiences shape identity. Renita reflects on repeatedly moving between India and Bahrain, adapting to new languages and schools, and overcoming challenges. She concludes that setbacks are merely chapters, and resilience, courage, kindness, humour, and adaptability help us grow. Renita is a confident, adaptable, and resilient student whose diverse experiences across cultures and schools have shaped her into an open-minded individual. She embraces change with positivity, humour, and courage. A thoughtful storyteller and keen observer, she reflects deeply on life’s experiences and draws meaningful lessons from them. Her ability to connect personal experiences with universal truths makes her a compelling speaker who inspires others to embrace change and write their own stories. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Curare è esserci | TIZIANO SCARPARO | TEDxVibo Valentia
recentItems.description: Nel suo talk al TEDx Vibo Valentia, Tiziano Scarparo ha raccontato la medicina come una scelta di responsabilità, cura e umanità. Partendo dalla sua esperienza professionale, ha portato sul palco una riflessione sul valore dello stare accanto alle persone nei momenti più delicati, mostrando come il benessere non riguardi solo il corpo, ma anche ascolto, fiducia e consapevolezza. Il suo intervento è stato un invito a prendersi cura di sé e degli altri con attenzione, equilibrio e rispetto, trasformando ogni scelta quotidiana in un passo verso una vita più sana e autentica. Tiziano Scarparo è medico chirurgo, medico nutrizionista e divulgatore, conosciuto per il suo lavoro nel campo della dietologia, della nutrizione e del digiuno intermittente. Laureato in Medicina e Chirurgia, ha approfondito il rapporto tra alimentazione, salute e benessere, costruendo un metodo basato su educazione alimentare, personalizzazione e sostenibilità dello stile di vita. Attraverso la sua attività professionale e divulgativa, accompagna le persone verso un rapporto più consapevole con il cibo, trasformando la nutrizione in uno strumento di cura, equilibrio e cambiamento quotidiano. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
